title: Vector triangles for coplanar equilibrium enrichment

evidence.role: Retrieves the two-condition equilibrium test that the vector-triangle method must not replace.

hints: Recall that equilibrium needs one condition about all forces and another about turning effects.
State each condition using the word resultant.

walkthrough.text: Separate translational balance from rotational balance. They are independent tests.
For translational balance, the vector sum of all forces must be zero, so the resultant force in every direction is zero.
For rotational balance, the sum of moments or torques about any point must be zero. Both statements are required.

ai_rubric.observable: States that the resultant force in any direction is zero
States that the resultant moment or torque about any point is zero

evidence.role: Diagnoses recognition of the closed head-to-tail construction demanded by the official scale-triangle leaf.

hints: Imagine walking along the arrows in order from tail to head.
A zero resultant leaves no displacement between the first and final points.

walkthrough.text: Vector addition is represented by placing each new arrow's tail at the previous arrow's head.
If the resultant is zero, the final head has no separation from the original tail.
The correct construction is therefore the closed head-to-tail polygon described by option B.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects B, identifying a closed head-to-tail force polygon as zero resultant force

evidence.role: Checks the direction and scale discipline needed for a valid closed triangle.

hints: A force vector keeps the same length and direction when moved on the page.
Ask which option changes only where the unchanged arrow chain begins.

walkthrough.text: Reversing, rotating or shortening an arrow changes the force vector represented.
Changing the cyclic order moves unchanged arrows head-to-tail without altering any magnitude or direction.
Option C is the only allowed change. The same three vectors still have a zero sum.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects C, preserving every force magnitude and direction while changing only the cyclic order

evidence.role: Combines the equilibrium-condition evidence with vector closure to diagnose overclaiming from a force diagram.

hints: Translate triangle closure into one of the two equilibrium conditions.
Consider whether the triangle contains any information about the forces' lines of action on a rigid body.

walkthrough.text: A closed triangle says that the vector sum of the three forces is zero.
It does not show where the forces act on an extended body, so it cannot establish their total turning effect.
Option A is correct: force balance is shown, while torque balance remains a separate check.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects A, distinguishing zero resultant force from the separate zero-torque condition

evidence.role: Transfers the official closed scale-triangle demand to an original perpendicular-force junction with a calculation from the completed triangle.

hints: Use the stated scale on each known force before adding the closing side.
After the drawing, identify the right triangle formed by the 36 N and 48 N sides.

walkthrough.text: Convert the known forces to scale lengths and place them head-to-tail in their stated directions.
Close the triangle with P from the final head to the original tail.
Use right-triangle geometry to obtain P's magnitude and the angle of its south-west direction.

evidence.role: Assesses a labelled, scaled, closed tip-to-tail triangle with a fresh direction pair.

hints: At 1.0 cm for 12 N, convert 36 N and 48 N to drawing lengths.
The arrow P must undo the combined east and north movement.

walkthrough.text: The 36 N east force has a scale length of 36/12 = 3.0 cm. Draw it east.
The 48 N north force has a scale length of 48/12 = 4.0 cm. Draw it north from the first arrow's head.
Draw P from the head of the 4.0 cm arrow back to the original tail. Label P and keep its arrowhead pointing towards the start.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws the 36 N and 48 N forces as 3.0 cm and 4.0 cm arrows in the correct east and north directions, placed head-to-tail
Draws and labels P as the closing arrow from the final head back to the original tail

evidence.role: Uses the geometry created by the evidence-grounded force-triangle construction.

hints: The two known sides are perpendicular.
P has the same magnitude as the resultant of the two known forces, but the opposite direction.

walkthrough.text: Use the perpendicular side lengths 36 N and 48 N in the completed force triangle.
Calculate $P=\sqrt{36^2+48^2}=\sqrt{3600}=60$ N.
Check that 60 N is longer than either perpendicular side but shorter than their 84 N sum.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses the right-angled force triangle to obtain P = 60 N

evidence.role: Extends the closed triangle to a precise direction with an original right-triangle ratio.

hints: P points back towards the original tail, so identify its quadrant before calculating the angle.
For an angle measured from west, compare the southward side with the westward side.

walkthrough.text: The closing arrow is opposite to the north-east resultant, so P points south-west.
For the angle theta from west, use $\tan\theta=48/36$.
$\theta=\tan^{-1}(48/36)=53.130...^\circ$, giving 53.1 degrees south of west.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses tan theta = 48/36 for the acute angle measured from west
Obtains a direction of 53.1 degrees south of west for P

evidence.role: Raises the official triangle demand to an original oblique system solved through component closure.

hints: Resolve only the oblique known force first.
The unknown force must cancel the combined horizontal and vertical totals separately.

walkthrough.text: Choose east and north as positive and resolve B with signs fixed by its north-west direction.
Add A and B component by component, then reverse both totals to obtain C.
Use the two perpendicular components of C to calculate its magnitude and direction.

evidence.role: Supplies the signed component route to the same force closure represented graphically in the official evidence.

hints: Force B points west and north, so its two components have opposite signs if east and north are positive.
Combine B's westward component with the 50 N east force before reporting the horizontal total.

walkthrough.text: Take east and north as positive. B has horizontal component $-80\cos60^\circ=-40.0$ N and vertical component $+80\sin60^\circ=+69.282...$ N.
Add A horizontally: $+50.0+(-40.0)=+10.0$ N, so the combined horizontal component is 10.0 N east.
A has no vertical component, so the combined vertical component is 69.3 N north.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the horizontal component of A plus B as 50 - 80 cos 60 degrees = 10.0 N east
Calculates the vertical component of A plus B as 80 sin 60 degrees = 69.3 N north

evidence.role: Computes the closing side of an original oblique equilibrium triangle.

hints: C must be the exact opposite of the combined force from part (a).
Use C's west and south components as perpendicular sides.

walkthrough.text: A plus B is 10.0 N east and 69.282... N north, so C must be 10.0 N west and 69.282... N south.
Check by adding C: the horizontal total becomes zero and the vertical total becomes zero.

ai_rubric.observable: Recognises that C has components 10.0 N west and 69.3 N south to close the force triangle
Calculates C = sqrt(10.0 squared + 69.3 squared) = 70.0 N

evidence.role: Requires a direction consistent with the computed closing components rather than a guessed diagram quadrant.

hints: C has a much larger southward component than westward component.
For an angle from south, divide the westward component by the southward component.

walkthrough.text: C points west and south. The requested acute angle starts from the south direction.
The complete direction is 8.21 degrees west of south. Its small angle agrees with the dominant southward component.

ai_rubric.observable: Uses tan theta = 10.0/69.3 for the acute angle measured from south
Obtains a direction of 8.21 degrees west of south for C

evidence.role: Combines the evidence-grounded moment route with a new three-force triangle while preserving the whole rigid-body dependency.

hints: Use the hinge as the pivot before attempting the force triangle.
After finding the cable tension, keep its physical direction unchanged when placing it head-to-tail with the weight.

walkthrough.text: Use rotational balance about the hinge to determine the cable tension.
Treat the weight, known tension and hinge reaction as the three sides of one closed force triangle.
Resolve the known forces to recover the magnitude and direction of the closing hinge reaction, then check both component totals.

evidence.role: Adapts the official angled-cable moment demand to fresh beam data and a different attachment point.

hints: The beam's weight acts 0.60 m from the hinge.
Only the vertical component of cable tension produces a moment about the hinge because the beam is horizontal.

walkthrough.text: Take moments about the hinge. The 240 N weight acts at the midpoint, so its clockwise moment is $240\times0.60=144$ N m.
The cable's vertical component is $T\sin30^\circ$ and acts 1.2 m from the hinge, so its anticlockwise moment is $(T\sin30^\circ)\times1.2$.
Set the moments equal: $(T\sin30^\circ)\times1.2=144$. Since $\sin30^\circ=0.5$, $0.60T=144$ and $T=240$ N.

ai_rubric.observable: Forms the clockwise weight moment about the hinge as 240 x 0.60 N m
Equates moments using (T sin 30 degrees) x 1.2 = 240 x 0.60
Obtains T = 240 N

evidence.role: Applies the official closed scale-triangle demand after a dependent moment result in an original beam context.

hints: Use the 240 N tension from part (a) and the 240 N downward weight.
The reaction must be drawn last in the direction that returns to the triangle's starting point.

walkthrough.text: Draw the 240 N weight vertically downward.
From its head, draw the 240 N cable tension at 30 degrees above the horizontal towards the wall, preserving the physical force direction.
Draw and label R from the tension arrow's head back to the original tail. The three arrows now form one closed head-to-tail triangle.

ai_rubric.observable: Draws the weight and cable tension with their correct directions and places the three force arrows head-to-tail
Draws and labels R as the closing side so that the vector triangle returns to its starting point

evidence.role: Completes the dependent rigid-body chain by turning the moment-derived tension into a numerical closing reaction.

hints: The cable tension has a leftward component and an upward component.
Choose the reaction components that make both the horizontal and vertical force totals zero.

walkthrough.text: For the 240 N cable tension, the horizontal component is $240\cos30^\circ=207.846...$ N left and the vertical component is $240\sin30^\circ=120$ N up.
After including the 240 N downward weight, the known-force total is 207.846... N left and 120 N down. R must therefore be 207.846... N right and 120 N up.
$R=\sqrt{207.846...^2+120^2}=240$ N and $\tan\theta=120/207.846...$, so $\theta=30.0^\circ$ above the horizontal towards the right.
Check: right and left components cancel, up and down components cancel, and part (a) already confirmed zero resultant torque.

deterministic_checks.accepted_direction: above the horizontal towards the right

ai_rubric.observable: Obtains hinge-reaction components of 240 cos 30 degrees = 208 N right and 240 - 240 sin 30 degrees = 120 N up
Calculates the hinge-reaction magnitude as 240 N
Gives the hinge-reaction direction as 30.0 degrees above the horizontal towards the right

quality_audit.originality: All learner prompts, contexts, values, calculations and planned figure briefs are original. No official wording, values or diagram geometry is reproduced.
quality_audit.scope: The package stays within three-force coplanar equilibrium, geometry or component recovery of an unknown force, and the already taught independent moment check.
quality_audit.evidence: The three mapped complete P2 questions, their official mark schemes and their enrichment records were reviewed. Only target leaves and necessary whole-question dependencies informed this package; unrelated deformation, spring, pressure and motion demands were excluded.
quality_audit.numerical_recomputation: All generated values were independently recomputed: q05 gives 60.0 N at 53.130102 degrees south of west; q06 gives combined components 10.0 N east and 69.282032 N north, then C = 70.0 N at 8.213211 degrees west of south; q07 gives T = 240.0 N and R components 207.846097 N right and 120.0 N up, hence R = 240.0 N at 30.0 degrees above horizontal.
quality_audit.dependency_audit: Exactly two learner-visible questions exercise declared dependency. q01 directly retrieves both equilibrium conditions from 9702_t04_cm02_l04. q07 combines the prior moment method and turning-effects module with the current closed force triangle.
quality_audit.visual_audit: Six note figures and three question figures are planned with specific teaching or assessment purposes. No image assets were generated, so all figure records remain planned and visual status is not_created.
